Coppock, Alexander. 2016. <b>Positive, Small, Homogeneous, and Durable: Political Persuasion in Response to Information</b>. NA.


# Abstract
This dissertation offers a theory of political persuasion rooted in a Bayesian model of information processing. I support this theory with the results of 20 survey experiments, conducted variously on samples of convenience, nationally representative samples, and samples of political elites. Deposited at Columbia University Academic Commons.
